title: All Audit Findings, Ranked
eyebrow: The full audit, the design loop deep dive, the usability audit and a hook friction pass, in one list · nothing changed yet

short.lead: This puts every finding from today in one list, ranked by harm. There are 20 from the full audit, 12 from the design loop deep dive and 9 from the usability audit. The other 5 are new, from running all 17 hooks against routine commands. The new pass found that a commit message mentioning rm -rf or push --force is refused, unstaging a file is refused, and git add can be blocked by the rerun counter. Seven findings are critical, because a program runs, data leaks or files are lost with no prompt. Eleven more block routine work. Blocks rank above lock bypasses because the only way past a block is to switch the whole check off.
short.hint: Tap a card to see the findings at that level.
items: H1: commit messages and echo text that mention rm -rf or push --force are refused. H2: git restore --staged and git reset HEAD on a file are refused, though both keep the edits. H3: git add was refused by the rerun counter after other commands had named the file. H4: each shell command starts 6 hook processes taking 347 to 490 ms, and each write starts 9 taking 424 to 636 ms. H5: .txt, .csv and .json files are locked like code.
7 findings: runs, leaks or loss with no prompt

A1 a commit runs any program. A11 autosave pushes untracked files, secrets included. D1 a GitHub comment can approve a stage. A3 /bin/rm and find -delete get past the delete guard. A4 checkout HEAD -- and switch -f discard edits. U5 git worktree remove --force is unguarded. A8 the installer can empty settings.json.
11 findings that push checks to be switched off

A5 cloud sessions can't commit to agent/ branches. U4 nothing can be deleted to free disk. U1 handoff repeats every approval. U2b: issues created by a script aren't counted. A6, H3 and U8: reading a script is treated as running it. U6 and H1: quoted text is treated as a command. H2: unstaging a file is refused. U7 the first cloud commit is refused three times. U2 approvals are saved only on push.

Level 3 (9): the model can step around the code lock, with shell writes (D10) the largest. Level 4 (13): approvals and tools give wrong answers but lose nothing. Level 5 (5): missing tests, added alongside each step, the time hooks take to run, and dead code.
Six steps, critical holes first. Each step becomes one feature with its own issues, and each fix lands with a verify.py test case.
Send "Design approved: audit fix order" with your pick under Choices, or tell me what to change.

changes: chg
Step 1: Close the critical holes
A1, A3, A4, U5, A11, A8 and D1.
Programs run, files are lost and outsiders can approve, all with no prompt.
Guard patterns widened, autosave adds only tracked and written files, the installer writes atomically, and four more relayed-message markers are added.
The only findings where harm happens without any mistake by you.
chg
Step 2: Stop blocking routine work
A5, A6 with H3, U6 with H1, H2 and U7.
Commits, reads, unstaging and cloud branches are refused.

agent/ is owned; only interpreter runs count as running a script; single-quoted text and heredocs with a quoted delimiter are skipped, but $(...) in double quotes is still checked; --staged is allowed; the hook sets the git identity.
Each of these blocks, left as it is, ends with someone switching a check off.
chg
Step 3: Fix handoff and full disk
U4, U1, U2 and U2b.
A handoff repeats every approval, and a full disk can't be cleared.
'Continue from: <branch>' and 'Issues for <feature>: #N'; folder deletes git or an install can undo; issue recording sees loops and gh api; approvals are pushed at once.
The two problems you named: the handoff repeating approvals, and the full disk.
chg
Steps 4 to 6: Side doors, approvals, tidying
Levels 3, 4 and 5.
The model can step around the lock, and some approvals move the wrong thing.
Side doors closed (D3, D4, A9, A7, D2, D9, A2), approvals checked (D5 to D8, U3), then tooling and dead code.
D10, the shell-write gap, stays with the restructure but gets its own issue.
choices: Which order should the fixes go in?
Critical first, then unblock routine work, then handoff and disk
Harm with no prompt goes first. The blocks come next because they get checks switched off.
Unblock routine work first, then critical
Faster day-to-day relief, but the critical holes stay open longer.
The two problems you named first, but it leaves the critical holes for later.
My suggestion is A, because step 1 is the only one where harm needs no mistake by you.

wrapup.summary: 45 separate findings in one ranked list (U8 is the same as A6): 7 critical, 11 that block work, 9 lock bypasses, 13 wrong results and 5 minor, with a six-step fix order.
wrapup.changing: Nothing has been changed. The list is in docs/audits/2026-11-05-combined-ranked.md, committed on the branch AjsAgent/audit-2026-11-05.
